answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to make every new identity cost real compute before it can join. Picture a field of meadow agents, each needing a small proof of work at admission, while a farm of fake identities would have to pay that cost again and again. Peers who grade each other's output can then spot the same operator reusing a velvet style of spam across identities, and a mesa of verified, costly identities stays trustworthy while the fakes lose money.
